title: report-intake chart values
description: Validated by helm BEFORE anything renders, on the coalesced values of every -f and --set. WHY it exists: a chart's values are an API and without a schema it is an untyped one, so `config.port: "9109"` or a `config.authmode` typo installs cleanly and the pod runs on a field's default. For AUTH_MODE that default is authentication disabled. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: encode the conditional refusals. Every `if/then` in this file would run BEFORE the template that already refuses the same combination, replacing a paragraph that names the failure with `must be at least 1 item` — and `.github/scripts/verify_chart_wiring.py` asserts several of those paragraphs by their words. So the schema types the VALUES and the templates refuse the COMBINATIONS; where a reader will expect a conditional and find none, a $comment says which guard owns it.

replicaCount.description: Safe above 1 — the retry sweep claims rows by a per-row conditional UPDATE against lease_expires_at, so the database arbitrates and one report cannot become two tickets. Above 1 needs a shared database; the image's sqlite default is per-Pod.

tag.description: Empty falls back to Chart.appVersion, which `helm package --app-version` sets from the release tag. A released chart therefore pins the exact version that built it without any values file naming one.

securityContext.$comment: Free-form on purpose: it is a Kubernetes SecurityContext and the API server validates it. runAsUser must stay 10001 unless the image changes — the Dockerfile creates that user and it is the one that can read the venv and write /data — but that is a fact about a pair of files, not a range a schema can state.

config.description: §2.4's environment surface. Every key here becomes one REPORT_INTAKE_* variable and every one of them is a field on report_intake.config.Settings — an equality asserted from both sides, because extra='ignore' makes a mismatch silent.

authMode.$comment: NO enum here, deliberately. `report-intake.validate` already refuses an unknown mode with a sentence explaining what each one is (disabled is loopback-only, not 'no auth'), and verify_chart_wiring.py asserts the rendered value against config.py's own AuthMode Literal, read from its AST. An enum here would run first and replace the explanation with a list.

allowedNetworks.$comment: Strings, not a CIDR pattern: a regex tight enough to be worth having would reject a legal IPv6 network, and rejecting a legal value is worse here than accepting a bad one — config.py parses each entry with strict=True at boot and the verifier does the same at PR time. Empty is legal at this layer; `mesh_or_turnstile` with an empty list is refused by the template, which explains why nothing could ever be mesh-verified.

corsOrigins.description: Browser origins allowed to POST a report — scheme, host and port, no trailing slash. Empty installs no CORS middleware at all; an empty allowlist is not an allowlist of everything.

trustClientIpHeader.description: Catches `--set config.trustClientIpHeader=yes`, which --set leaves as a string: the ConfigMap would render `"yes"`, pydantic would reject it, and the pod would CrashLoop on a value that looked right in the values file.

ticketSink.$comment: NO enum, and this one is a contradiction the schema must not introduce rather than a message it must not preempt. config.py declares ticket_sink as a plain string on purpose so that adding an adapter is one line in delivery/registry.SINKS — not an edit to config, a chart and a schema at once. `delivery.registry.build_sink` is the authority and refuses an unknown name at boot.

linearTeamId.$comment: Empty is legal — it is inert unless ticketSink names linear, and the template refuses that combination with a message about teamId being a UUID rather than a key like OME.

linearApiUrl.description: Linear's one GraphQL endpoint. The scheme check is the point: the ConfigMap renders this key in every install, so a value missing `https://` overrides config.py's default and fails at request time — on the sink, per report, not at boot.

deliveryTimeoutS.$comment: No maximum here, though one exists: main._check_delivery_timeout refuses a value whose worst-case inline attempt is not shorter than retry.CLAIM_GRACE, because a sweeper on another replica would then claim a report the request path is still delivering and file one bug as two tickets. That bound is arithmetic over two constants in two modules; copying it here would make a third place that can drift, and a stale copy would refuse a legal value. Spec §2.2's number is 3.

anonRate.description: The service-side backstop, not spec §7's per-caller edge limit — its key is the TCP peer, and in a cluster that is the mesh proxy on every request. The per-caller half is gateway.public.rateLimit.
anonRate.$comment: minimum 1 on all four mirrors config.py's `Field(ge=1)` exactly — each is a divisor or a capacity, so zero is a division by zero inside the bucket or a service that admits nobody. A mirror of a per-field bound is not the conditional-refusal case: nothing renders a better message for it, and this one moves the failure from a CrashLoop to the install.

forwardedAllowIps.$comment: A comma list of addresses and CIDRs — uvicorn's own variable, not a Settings field. No pattern excluding `*`: the template refuses that value with the paragraph explaining that uvicorn would then rewrite request.client.host from a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For for every peer, and verify_chart_wiring.py asserts that refusal by its words. minLength 1 only, because an empty value silently returns uvicorn to its own default instead of the posture the manifest states.

existingSecret.$comment: No minLength: `report-intake.databaseEnv` already `required`s it with a message saying the URL carries a password and is never a chart value.

EMPTY IS LEGAL AND MUST STAY LEGAL: values-cloud.yaml ships `enabled: true` with this empty on purpose, so the render stops until an install names the Secret. A minLength here — even inside an `if enabled` — would make `helm template -f values-cloud.yaml` fail with a schema error instead of the Deployment's `required`, which explains that siteverify would reject this service's own credentials and answer every anonymous report 503.

linear.description: Where the Linear API key comes from IF this deployment ever files into Linear directly. There is deliberately no `enabled` flag — config.ticketSink is the switch, and a second one could disagree with it.

existingSecret.$comment: No minLength for the same reason as turnstile's: verify_chart_wiring.py sets it EMPTY to prove the render refuses ticketSink=linear without it, and that refusal names CLAUDE.md rule 9 and OME-976. A schema error would preempt the one message in this chart that tells an operator the choice is governed by a repo rule.

gateway.description: Gateway API, not Ingress: the header manipulation this service's identity model rests on is a typed filters: field on an HTTPRoute. Prerequisites, none installed here — the Gateway API CRDs, a GatewayClass, and Envoy Gateway specifically for SecurityPolicy and BackendTrafficPolicy.

name.$comment: Empty is legal here and refused at render by the two routes' `required`. A chart cannot know the name of an object it does not install.

timeouts.$comment: Gateway API Duration, matching the engine chart's spelling. `30` without a unit is a schema error here rather than an HTTPRoute the controller rejects after install.

rateLimit.description: Spec §7's per-caller edge rate limit, as an Envoy BackendTrafficPolicy on the public route only. Off by default; on in values-cloud.yaml. It needs Envoy Gateway's Redis-backed rate-limit service and a ClientTrafficPolicy establishing the real client address — neither installable here, and both fail open.

unit.description: Envoy Gateway's RateLimitUnit. An enum here rather than in a template guard because nothing else refuses it: `unit: hour` renders a policy the controller rejects after install, on a hostname that is this repo's first unauthenticated write.

sourceCIDRs.$comment: One rule per entry, each bucketing per address inside it. An empty list is refused by `report-intake.validate`, which explains that a policy with no rules renders, reports Accepted, and limits nothing.

teamDomain.description: `<team>.cloudflareaccess.com` — a bare host. The issuer and the JWKS URL are both derived from it, so a value carrying a scheme or a path renders `https://https://…/cdn-cgi/access/certs` and the JWT filter fetches nothing.

service.$comment: ExternalName is excluded rather than omitted: this Service carries a selector, and an ExternalName Service with one is rejected by the API server — after `helm upgrade` has reported success.

livenessProbe.$comment: Free-form, and the constraint that matters is not expressible here: liveness must point at /healthz, which never touches storage, and readiness at /readyz, which queries the reports TABLE. A liveness probe that can fail for an external reason turns one bad database into a restart loop across every replica. verify_chart_wiring.py asserts both paths and that they differ.

migration.description: The schema, applied as a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook. This service never migrates itself: auto-migrating means every replica racing the same DDL on a fresh database.

networkPolicy.description: Who may reach this Service. Under authMode: mesh_or_turnstile this is not hardening layered on the authentication boundary — the in-process peer check authenticates a NETWORK, so this is what makes that network the mesh gateway rather than every pod in the cluster.
networkPolicy.$comment: No `if enabled then minItems` on the peer lists: three values feed one peer set, so the real condition is that their UNION is non-empty — which is what networkpolicy.yaml checks, with a message saying an ingress rule with no `from:` admits every source. verify_chart_wiring.py asserts that message.

$comment: additionalProperties:false is the half of this file that earns its keep. `config.authmode`, a `gateway.hostnames` copied from the engine chart, a `podDisruptionBudget` block left behind after a template was deleted — each is accepted silently by Helm and by `extra='ignore'` downstream, and each leaves the pod on a default while the values file says otherwise. `global` is allowed because Helm injects it for subcharts.
